chunks.text: Definition: A neural network is a computational model inspired by the human brain, composed of layers of interconnected nodes that learn to map inputs to outputs.
Claim: Backpropagation computes gradients by applying the chain rule across layers, allowing the network to update weights in the direction that minimizes the loss function.
Example: If a transformer model attends more strongly to certain tokens when predicting the next word, this selective focus is an example of the attention mechanism in action.
Support: Batch normalization stabilizes training by normalizing activations across the batch dimension, reducing internal covariate shift and allowing higher learning rates.
